old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a clear plastic bag partially covering a cluster of green leaves. The bag is slightly crumpled, allowing some light to filter through, creating a soft, diffused illumination on the leaves beneath. Water droplets are visible on both the bag and the leaves, indicating recent rain or dew. The camera remains stationary, focusing on the interaction between the bag and the leaves. The text overlay at the bottom of the frame reads, "These will start to run down the sides of the bag and collect in the lowest point," suggesting an educational or instructional purpose, possibly explaining how water collects in a bag after rainfall. The overall scene is serene and natural, emphasizing the simple yet intricate details of the environment.

caption: The video captures a close-up view of several green, lance-shaped leaves enclosed behind a transparent plastic sheet whose inner surface is coated with condensation. A fine mist of tiny droplets spreads across the upper-left region, while scattered larger beads and a few elongated drips cling to the film, including one prominent hanging droplet near the right-center. Throughout the excerpt the leaves, stems, and droplet pattern remain fixed in place, with no detectable movement or camera shift. The only visible change is a white sans-serif caption that gradually emerges over the lower portion of the image. It is absent at first, becomes faintly legible, and then settles into full opacity, reading that the droplets will run down the sides of the bag and collect in the lowest point. That described motion is not shown within this segment; the physical scene stays static while the overlay text fades in and holds steady.

If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
